"In accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, if you require a

310-952-1720 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting.” (Government Code Section
54954.2)
PUBLIC INFORMATION

The public may address the members of the City Council on any matters within the
jurisdiction of the City Council or on any items on the agenda of the City Council
during the designated public comment periods. There will be two Oral
Communication sessions: one for Agendized Items (comment about items ON the
agenda) and the other for non-Agendized items (comment about items NOT on the
Agenda). The Oral Communications portion of the agenda is limited to a duration of
one hour unless otherwise approved by the City Council. Comment time is normally
3 minutes depending on the number of speakers.

Because of the threat of COVID-19 (the “Coronavirus”) you are urged to take all
appropriate health safety precautions. Wearing masks is not required but is highly
recommended while inside Carson City Hall. Temperatures will be checked for those
experiencing any symptoms of COVID-19, prior to entering the City Hall.

CALL TO ORDER: CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY/HOUSING AUTHORITY (5:00 pm) Absent: Councilmember Rojas (excused absence, at work) 
Present: Councilmember Dear, Hicks, Mayor Pro-Tem Hilton, Mayor Davis-Holmes


ROLL CALL (CITY CLERK): Councilmember Dear

FLAG SALUTE:  Mayor Pro-Tem Hilton

INVOCATION: none

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR MATTERS LISTED ON THE AGENDA (MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC) (LIMITED TO ONE HOUR) Cristine Gaiennie and Tarik Rahmani introduced RCS Consultants who are conducting the fee study.
The fee study began in 2019. The city has not had a fee study conducted since 2008. 

1:43pm MPT steps away from meeting
1:59pm Assistant City Manager John Raymond steps away from meeting 
MPT returned to the meeting at 2:13pm 

The consultants are recommending full recovery but council is recommending that the fees with increases be phased in over a two year period. Tarik and the consultants will come back with data to show as the council requested. 

Tarik also mentioned that there will be a separate meeting to discuss Community Services fees. It will be a public hearing. 

Council discussed not increasing fees that impact small businesses and home businesses versus large businesses. 

City Manager David Roberts mentioned that the fireworks fee is being recommended to be increased from $25 to $60 but the mayor decided that the fee should remain the same. 

City Manager stepped away from meeting at 2:21pm
